question: GQ-008
subject: the retention I set is live and does nothing — corrected by measurement
what_i_claimed_yesterday: "log_retention_days 365 -> 3, verified against the running process. It bounds future growth."
what_was_true: the setting is live. The claim that it bounds growth was never tested.

measured_six_hours_later.oldest_row: 2026-08-01, 3.15 days — past the threshold, still present
measured_six_hours_later.verdict: configured, not enforced. Nothing evicts. A retention that never runs is worse than none because it reads as solved.

built: scripts/enforce-log-retention.sh — npm run log:enforce-retention, dry-run by default
why_this_is_not_a_C1_violation: C1 protects DATA THE LIBRARY HOLDS. This is a gateway request log whose load-bearing columns are already preserved on the vault and verified before every run. The script refuses to delete unless the slice answers 5/5 both before AND after a refresh.

an_ordering_bug_i_caught_before_applying.what: my first version verified the EXISTING slice, then deleted
an_ordering_bug_i_caught_before_applying.why_wrong: that proves the old slice still answers — it says nothing about the rows about to be deleted
an_ordering_bug_i_caught_before_applying.the_evidence: of the 136 rows past the window, 52 were CodexOpenAI and 44 Minimax — exactly the providers all five derivations read
an_ordering_bug_i_caught_before_applying.fix: refresh the slice to include them, re-verify, and only then delete

result.the_honest_part: the file GREW despite a VACUUM. Those 136 rows were the oldest and smallest, and live traffic during the rebuild outpaced what they freed. Row-count retention does not control this file — size does. I am recording that rather than reporting a 136-row deletion as a disk win.

the_architecture_held.note: deleting the live rows cost nothing because the numbers were already preserved. The slice built yesterday did exactly what it was for.
